# The relation disjoint of IEEE 1788, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_rel_disjoint_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $X$ and $Y$ have no member in common, $X = [x_l, x_u]$ and $Y = [y_l, y_u]$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \cap Y = \emptyset.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $y_l = y_{l0} + y_{l1}$, $y_u = y_{u0} + y_{u1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ieee1788::disjoint(X, Y)` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `bool` | `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $Y = [y_l, y_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $y_l = +\infty$ and $y_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $y_l \le y_u$, $y_l < +\infty$, $y_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $X$ and $Y$ have no member in common: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_rel_disjoint_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_rel_disjoint_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_rel_disjoint_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the stored bounds compared, and tests of emptiness (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_rel_disjoint_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_rel_disjoint_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md).

```
# The relation disjoint of IEEE 1788 of two intervals with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md,
# "Comparisons", the relations of IEEE 1788, and "IEEE 1788"): X and Y have no member in common. An
# empty operand is disjoint from everything; otherwise x_u < y_l or y_u < x_l. Exact. For every
# precision.

ex = eq(xl0, const inf)
ey = eq(yl0, const inf)
ee = or(ex, ey)
da = lt_2_2(xu0, xu1, yl0, yl1)
db = lt_2_2(yu0, yu1, xl0, xl1)
dd = or(da, db)
m  = or(ee, dd)
```
